newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U to apply for FDA approval of incontinence drug.
newsitem.headline: P&U to apply for FDA approval of incontinence drug.

text.p: Swedish/U.S drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Monday it planned to apply today for approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its incontinence drug Detrusitol.
"The application will be filed today," Pharmacia & Upjohn spokesman Soren Densjo told Reuters. "Everything is on its way to the FDA."
Densjo did not want to speculate on how long it would take the FDA to consider the application.
Detrusitol, also known as Tolterodine, and anti-glaucoma agent Xalatan are P&U's drugs with the most potential in the company's current portfolio.
"Xalatan and Detrusitol will be of very large importance for future development," Densjo said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn filed for approval for Detrusitol from the Swedish drug authorities just before year-end 1996.
